text: Pair odd vertices by shortest paths.

The Chinese postman problem (中国邮路问题): the shortest closed walk that uses every edge of a connected undirected graph at least once. If every degree is even, the answer is the total weight (an Euler circuit, 拓展篇第17章). Otherwise some edges are walked twice: pair up the odd-degree vertices (there is an even number of them) with the smallest total shortest-path distance, and add that.

Pairing odd vertices = minimum-weight perfect matching on their shortest-path distances. With up to about 20 odd vertices, a bitmask DP matches them (always pair the lowest unmatched vertex); in general it needs weighted blossom. The directed version is a min-cost flow on the in/out-degree imbalance.

SJ theorem; a table of rare topics.

Misère and Anti-SG games (Anti-SG / SJ 定理): in "last player to move loses" versions, plain SG fails. For sums of games where a position with SG = 0 everywhere has no move, the first player wins iff either (the SG of the whole sum ≠ 0 and some single game has SG > 1) or (the sum's SG = 0 and no single game has SG > 1). Anti-Nim (拓展篇第10章) is the special case.

Other game patterns that appear at NOI: "every-SG" (players must move in every component, decided by the longest finishing time), games on graphs solved by retrograde analysis (BFS backwards from final positions, counting remaining moves per state), and partisan games where surreal-number values replace SG values (rare).

Inspect files; exact for easy ones, search for the rest.

Output-only tasks (提交答案题): you get the input files and submit outputs, often scored by quality. There is no time limit, so the strategy is different: look at each input first (many are special: a tree, a path, tiny n), solve the easy ones exactly, then run search or heuristics (simulated annealing 第24章 , random restarts, local search) on the rest for hours on your own machine.

Write a checker that scores your output before trying to improve it, keep the best output of every file, and spend effort where the score gap is largest. Hand-made constructions and visualising the input often beat a general algorithm on special files.

Green Hackenbush on trees (树上删边游戏): a rooted tree; a move deletes an edge, and everything no longer connected to the root disappears; who cannot move loses. Its SG value: SG(u) = XOR over children v of (SG(v) + 1), leaves 0. A chain of length k is a Nim heap of size k, and the "+1" puts the edge above a subtree on top of it like a stalk.

Colon principle: a subtree can be replaced by a chain with the same SG value. For graphs with cycles (fusion principle) an even cycle becomes a single vertex and an odd cycle a vertex with one extra edge, after which the tree rule applies. Sums of several trees: XOR their root values (拓展篇 SG).
